title: UBC Library FAQs
content_markdown:
Reactivating library access may mean renewing an account to borrow physical materials, and, in some cases may also mean renewing eResource access via OpenAthens:

-   **UBC Students, Faculty \(including Emeriti\) and Staff**: Users with an active appointment in Workday do not need to renew library access; physical borrowing and eResources access are renewed automatically as long as your status in Workday remains active\. 
-   **Alumni**: Alumni who have [applied for access to physical borrowing at the library](https://alumni.ubc.ca/services/library/) do not need to renew their library account\. Alumni [with an active OpenAthens account](https://guides.library.ubc.ca/connect/openathens/alumni) will receive an automated renewal reminder every 5 years\.
-   **Affiliated Staff**: Staff and Faculty who work at any of UBC's affiliated colleges \(Corpus Christi College and St\. Mark’s College; Regent College; Carey College; Vancouver School of Theology\) renew their physical borrowing and eResources access yearly, following the academic calendar\. Accounts will expire on September 15th of each year\.
-   **Faculty Authorized Users**: Faculty Authorized Users must renew their accounts \(physical borrowing and eResources access\) yearly, following the academic calendar\. Accounts will expire on September 15th of each year\. 
-   **Reciprocal Borrowing**: UBC and non\-UBC students requesting Reciprocal Borrowing accounts must renew yearly, following the academic calendar\. Accounts will expire on September 15th of each year\. Note that Reciprocal Borrowing for non\-UBC students does not include remote access to eResources\. 
-   **Community Users**: Community users receive physical borrowing privileges\. Most Community accounts are valid 1 year \(or less\) from the date of issue\.  Note that Community users do not receive remote access to eResources\. 
-   **Retired Staff**: Retired staff receive physical borrowing privileges\. Retired staff must have a ‘retired’ status in Workday\. Retired staff with a ‘retired’ status in Workday can [request a Retired Staff UBCCard](https://ubccard.ubc.ca/obtaining-a-ubccard/emeritus-retired-staff) to activate their physical borrowing privileges\. Note that Retired Staff do not receive remote access to eResources\.

Any users looking to renew or reactivate their library privileges should fill out an [Ask Us form](https://ask.library.ubc.ca/ask/)\.

Yes, you can view books from a library storage location \(PARC or ASRS\), even if you do not have a library card\! Note that materials in transit from storage locations often take several days and may not be available same\-day\. It is strongly recommended that users without a library card [contact UBC library](https://answers.library.ubc.ca/askus/) to request items from storage before coming to campus\. 

-   **PARC materials** \- contact [Koerner Library](https://koerner.library.ubc.ca/) to request items from PARC\. Items from PARC may take several days to reach Koerner Library\. Koerner Library staff will contact you when the items have arrived\. 
-   **ASRS materials** \- contact the [Music, Art and Architecture Library](https://maa.library.ubc.ca/) \(MAA\)\. Items from the ASRS may take several hours to several days to reach MAA\. MAA staff will contact you when the items have arrived\.  

Storage items are available for patrons without a library card to view in\-library only\. 

Users **with** a library card can follow the steps outlined on the [Library's Access Storage](https://services.library.ubc.ca/borrowing-services/storage/#fragment-a750fa8566bf75e9a6d930107eaa35ba-0) page to request materials\.

title: UBC Library FAQs
content_markdown:
The **General tab uses Summon**, a discovery tool that searches across many library resources at once\.

The other tabs \(Books & Media, Indexes and Databases, Journal Titles\) do not use Summon\. Instead, they connect to separate library systems designed for specific purposes\.

-   Use the **Books & Media** tab to search the UBC Library Catalogue for books and other catalogue materials\. 
-   Use the **Indexes & Databases** tab to locate subject\-specific research databases\.
-   Use the **Journal Titles** tab to look up a specific journal by title\.

Because these tabs search different systems, results may vary depending on which tab you use\.

Visit [How to Search Summon](https://guides.library.ubc.ca/summonhelp) for more details

title: UBC Library FAQs
content_markdown:
UBC Library provides many services for researchers\. This list is not comprehensive, but intended to connect researchers with key contacts in the library:

-   [Subject librarians](https://directory.library.ubc.ca/subjectlibrarians/) provide individualized support with many aspects of the research lifecycle
-   [Borrowing services](https://services.library.ubc.ca/borrowing-services/get-library-access/faculty/) are available to all researchers and there are options for visiting scholar access
-   The [Scholarly Communications Office](https://scholcomm.ubc.ca/?login) at UBC Vancouver provides support for journal discounts, open publishing, copyright and related topics
-   The [Research Commons](https://researchcommons.library.ubc.ca/?login) is a multidisciplinary hub that provides access to services and expertise in digital scholarship, geospatial information systems \(GIS\), data services, research data management \(RDM\), and citation management
-   The [Centre for Scholarly Communication](https://csc.ok.ubc.ca/) at UBC Okanagan, provide support for journal discounts, open publishing, copyright and related topics, data services, research data management \(RDM\), and citation management
-   Visit the [Research Data Management](https://rdm.ubc.ca/) website for data management services
-   Visit the [Knowledge Synthesis Service](https://knowledgesynthesis.library.ubc.ca/?login) website for two tiers of service which support different types of reviews
-   Visit the [cIRcle](https://circle.ubc.ca/?login) website to review options for depositing research outputs at UBC Library

UBC Library supports two curated repositories that meet most funder and publisher requirements for data deposit, increasingly mandated by funders like the Tri\-Agencies:

-   [UBC Dataverse Collection \(Borealis\)](https://researchdata.library.ubc.ca/deposit/dataverse): a national repository for more than 90 Canadian institutions, curated by UBC Library\. Best for small to medium\-sized datasets; supports DOI assignment, access controls, and FAIR principles\.
-   [Federated Research Data Repository \(FRDR\)](https://researchdata.library.ubc.ca/deposit/frdr/): a national platform curated by the Digital Research Alliance of Canada, designed for large\-scale datasets \(terabytes\)\.

UBC Library can also help identify discipline\-specific repositories\. Visit the [Deposit](https://researchdata.library.ubc.ca/deposit/) page or contact [research\.data@ubc\.ca](mailto:research.data@ubc.ca) to request a consultation\.

title: UBC Library FAQs
content_markdown:
UBC Library provides two types of accounts, one for borrowing items \(books, media, laptops\) and another for logging into online resources\. Figuring out what is going on can be a bit complicated\! 

**Library Account for Borrowing and Requesting Items**

Login to your [Library Account](https://services.library.ubc.ca/borrowing-services/library-account/) to view messages related to borrowing items\. You may have items that are overdue or lost which can lead to your account being blocked\. This will impact your ability to: borrow items at a circulation desk, renew items online, recall items that another user has borrowed, or request items through the document delivery service, interlibrary loan, or from our storage facilities \(ASRS, PARC\)\. 

Connect with our support team to resolve this issue\. You can complete an [Ask Us form](https://ask.library.ubc.ca/ask/), call our main support lines \(Vancouver: 604\-822\-2406/ Okanagan: 250\-807\-9107\), or visit [any location\.](https://hours.library.ubc.ca/) 

**Library Account for Online Resources**

UBC Library uses *OpenAthens* as a secure login service for digital, licensed resources \(books, journals, media, data\)\. 

All current UBC students, staff and faculty will automatically be able to use their CWL to login through OpenAthens to access the resources available to them\.

-   If you forgot your password or need to recover MFA access, [visit UBC IT\.](https://it.ubc.ca/services/accounts-passwords/campus-wide-login-cwl/problems-your-cwl)
-   If you cannot access any resources then complete an [Ask Us form](https://ask.library.ubc.ca/ask/)

For Alumni, Emeriti, Faculty Authorized Users and Affiliated College employees, please view our [full account documentation](https://guides.library.ubc.ca/connect/openathens) for access options\. Follow the details instructions for access that require you to login [through this link](https://openathens.library.ubc.ca/) before navigating to a licensed resource\. If your login is not working, submit an [Ask Us form](https://ask.library.ubc.ca/ask/)\.

title: UBC Library FAQs

You can request expedited access to items the [library catalogue \(OPAC\)](https://webcat1.library.ubc.ca/vwebv/searchBasic?) that have a status message of: In Process, On Order, and Pre\-Order Process\.   
  
Depending on the exact stage of receiving, processing and cataloguing that the item is in, we may or may not be able to increase the speed of delivery\.  

If we can rush the delivery of the item to you, it will be sent to the library location listed in the library catalogue record, and the contact information collected in this form will be used to notify you when the item is available\. Due to the variation in processing stages, we cannot estimate a delivery timeline\. 

Note: If a physical item in the catalogue has a call number displayed, it is already on its way to the library location and cannot be further rushed\.

Complete [this form to place rush item request](https://ask.library.ubc.ca/rushrequest/)

title: UBC Library FAQs

UBC Library cardholders can request library materials via UBC's Document Delivery \(DocDel\) service \- this service retrieves library materials for you\. 

The most common use of this service is book and article delivery between UBC campuses \(eg\. UBC Point Grey, UBC Robson Square, UBC Okanagan, and UBC teaching hospitals: BMB and BCCW Learning Commons\)\. 

DocDel also serves UBC undergraduate students and faculty in the Island Medical Program or Northern Medical Program, [distance education students](https://services.library.ubc.ca/borrowing-services/get-library-access/registering-for-distance-learning-library-services/), and students who qualify for [Enhanced Library Services](https://services.library.ubc.ca/borrowing-services/get-library-access/enhanced/)\. 

For more information, including details on fees attached to some DocDel services and DocDel contacts, please review the Library's [DocDel guide](https://services.library.ubc.ca/borrowing-services/docdel/#WhatisUBCDocDel-0)\.

title: UBC Library FAQs
content_markdown:
**Does UBC Preservation offer basic collection care recommendations?**

It’s inevitable that books and other information resources will deteriorate over time\. However, there are several simple steps that can help extend the life of a collection, including proper shelving and handling practices, food and beverage control, pest management, and prompt response to water damage\. This [UBC Library Collections Care document](https://technicalservices.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2012/05/WhiteCollectionsCarePowerPoint_Staff_20120724.pdf) provides an introduction to basic preservation recommendations\.

**Can UBC Preservation repair my family heirloom or rare book?**

Due to staffing and program priorities, the UBC Preservation Unit is only able to treat materials held in UBC Library collections and does not have the capacity to accept privately owned items for repair or conservation\.

**Can UBC Preservation recommend a private local conservator or bookbinder to restore the item?**

To find a conservator in your area, consult the [directory](https://capc-acrp.ca/en/conservators?___) maintained by the Canadian Association of Professional Conservators \(CAPC\), which can be searched by city and specialization\.

CAPC also provides resources on [selecting and working with a conservator](https://capc-acrp.ca/en/what-is-conservation/selecting-a-conservator)\.

To find a bookbinder or book repair specialist, please visit the Canadian Bookbinders and Book Artists Guild \(CBBAG\) for [conservation and repair resources](https://www.cbbag.ca/restoration-repair-faqs)\.

**Does** **UBC Preservation** **teach bookbinding, book repair, conservation, or collection care?**

Not at this time\. For bookbinding workshops, the Canadian Bookbinders and Book Artists Guild Lower Mainland chapter maintains an up\-to\-date list of both in\-person and online [workshops](https://vanbookarts.wordpress.com/)\.

UBC Preservation may occasionally offer presentations or outreach sessions related to collections care, which will be listed on the [UBC Library events calendar](https://libcal.library.ubc.ca/calendar/vancouver)\.

**Can** **UBC Preservation** **provide preservation advice for small community archives or personal collections?**

UBC Preservation may be able to offer informal preservation guidance for small community archives or personal collections, depending on staff availability\. Please contact the Conservator at 604\-822\-3441 to discuss your request\.

**Does** **UBC Preservation** **offer tours of the Conservation Space?**

At this time, the Conservation Space is not open for public tours\.

**Does** **UBC Preservation** **have any resources or advice about preparing for or responding to a library or collections disaster \(e\.g\. fire, flood, etc\.\)?**

UBC Preservation may be able to provide general advice about collections emergencies or disaster response by phone or email, depending on staff availability\. Please contact the Conservator at 604\-822\-3441 for more information\.

The [BC Heritage Emergency Response Network \(BC HERN\)](https://bchern.ca/what-is-bc-hern/) offers training, resources, and emergency support for cultural institutions and collections affected by disasters or localized emergencies\.

For collections emergencies, contact the Canadian Conservation Institute \(CCI\) 24\-hour emergency response line at 1\-866\-998\-3721\.

title: UBC Library FAQs
content_markdown:
Users will need to log in with either their CWLs or OpenAthens accounts in order to view online journals and access databases\. To log in, navigate to the [library home page](https://www.library.ubc.ca/) and click "Login" and select the "OpenAthens Login" button on the right hand side of the page\.

[OpenAthens Login button on the Library home page Login menu](https://d1qywhc7l90rsa.cloudfront.net/accounts/156391/images/OA.png)

If you are a current student, staff or faculty member, log in with your CWL\. Other users should log in with their OpenAthens accounts\. Not all OpenAthens accounts provide access to online resources remotely; for more information, review the [Connect to Library Resources guide](https://guides.library.ubc.ca/connect/general)\.

Note: Alumni can log in with a CWL to access select resources\. Please see [our FAQ about Alumni resources](https://answers.library.ubc.ca/askus/faq/215678) for more information\. 

Users can also log in via the Summon search page by clicking "Log in" on the top right of the results page:  

[Log in button on the Summon search page](https://d1qywhc7l90rsa.cloudfront.net/accounts/156391/images/Summon.png)

Logging in will show all available results, and provide access to online resources\. 

For assistance [locating journal articles](https://guides.library.ubc.ca/JournalArticles) or [navigating databases](https://guides.library.ubc.ca/library_tutorial/searching#s-lg-box-16492432), review the linked guides or reach out to your [Subject Librarian](https://directory.library.ubc.ca/subjectlibrarians/)\. 

If you have followed these steps and are unable to access online resources, submit an [Ask Us form](https://ask.library.ubc.ca/ask/)\.

title: UBC Library FAQs
content_markdown:
If you know the title of the article, you can begin by searching for it in [Summon](https://ubc.summon.serialssolutions.com/#!/search?pn=1&ho=t&include.ft.matches=f&l=en&q=)\. Enter the main title using quotation marks to search for those exact words\. If needed, select the Journal Articles filter listed under Content Type\. 

[Summon search of "The science of literature reviews" with Journal Articles selected under Content Type\.](https://d1qywhc7l90rsa.cloudfront.net/accounts/80416/images/FAQ_SummonArticleSearch.png)

If you have trouble finding the article or want to make sure we have a particular journal, search for a [journal by title](https://search.library.ubc.ca/#journals)\. Under journal details, select a holding \(via the hyperlink\) for the relevant dates\. Then navigate to the correct volume or issue\. This is also a good way to browse a journal's publications\. 

[Journal search showing the holdings of AlterNative : An International Journal of Indigenous Peoples](https://d1qywhc7l90rsa.cloudfront.net/accounts/80416/images/FAQ_JournalSearchExample.png)

If you are not looking for a specific journal article, but need support finding articles related to a specific research topic contact your [subject librarian](https://directory.library.ubc.ca/subjectlibrarians/)\.

UBC Library understands the value of persistent identifiers \(PIDs\) in facilitating long\-lasting digital reference to an object, contributor, or organization\. UBC offers supports and services for many types of PIDs\. 

Learn more on the [Persistent Identifier](https://guides.library.ubc.ca/PIDS "https://guides.library.ubc.ca/PIDS") guide about author, object, and institutional level identifiers\. 

Certain UBC departments are eligible to request UBC ISBN's from the Library for departmental publications\. Visit the [ISBN request form](https://ask.library.ubc.ca/isbnrequest/) for more details about this service\.

title: UBC Library FAQs
content_markdown:
UBC Library provides many services for instructors\. This list is not comprehensive, but intended to connect instructors with key contacts in the library:

-   [Subject librarians](https://directory.library.ubc.ca/subjectlibrarians/) provide support with many aspects of teaching and learning
-   [Borrowing services](https://services.library.ubc.ca/borrowing-services/get-library-access/faculty/) are available to all instructors
-   [Library Online Course Reserves \(LOCR\)](https://services.library.ubc.ca/borrowing-services/using-course-reserves/) allows instructors to create a single list with all the course materials\.
    -   Easily add articles, books, web links and media resources or request the Library to add items via the [Syllabus Service](https://services.library.ubc.ca/borrowing-services/using-course-reserves/#fragment-cc8b788e2107211a05cdccf71c302c69-1)
    -   Request the Library to create PDFs of book chapters or upload your own
    -   Get a hyperlink for the course materials that is accessible \(only\) to students enrolled in your course
    -   Reactivate readings in future terms quickly
-   Visit the [Scholarly Communication Open Education](https://scholcomm.ubc.ca/open-scholarship/open-education/) page for information and support with open educational resources \(OERs\)
-   Visit the [Copyright Office](https://copyright.ubc.ca/instructors/) website for resources intended to assist faculty members in applying copyright requirements in a classroom setting
-   Visit the [cIRcle](https://circle.ubc.ca/?login) website to review options for depositing teaching outputs at UBC Library
-   Visit the [Research Data Management](https://researchdata.library.ubc.ca/) website for resources and guidance related to finding, managing, and depositing research data\.

title: UBC Library FAQs
content_markdown:
UBC Library provides [bookable study spaces](https://services.library.ubc.ca/facilities/bookable-study-spaces/) in many of our library locations\.

Email notifications are sent to confirm your booking and contain a link to cancel your booking\. Depending on how you use UBC email systems, you may receive the notification at:

-   the email viewable through [myaccount\.ubc\.ca](https://www.myaccount.ubc.ca/myAccount/)
-   or your [student UBC email](http://it.ubc.ca/services/email-voice-internet/ubc-student-email-service)
-   or your [UBC employee email](http://it.ubc.ca/services/email-voice-internet/ubc-faculty-staff-email-fasmail)

Please note the email in use by this system when you confirm the booking, as the address cannot be updated\.

If you are an active UBC employee the library booking system will automatically use your business email\.  Within the library booking system, if you are attempting to: **Book a study room**, **Book an appointment**, or **Register for an event** and your email address is appearing as an **@ubc\.ca** or **@mail\.ubc\.ca** address, you are a current UBC staff member\.

If you are no longer able to access your email, and you cannot access your email notifications, please submit an [Ask Us form](https://ask.library.ubc.ca/ask/) and we will aim to get back to you within 24 hours, Monday through Friday\.

title: UBC Library FAQs
content_markdown:
A [Data Management Plan](https://researchdata.library.ubc.ca/plan/) \(DMP\) is a document outlining how you will organize, store, back up, and share your research data throughout your project\. DMPs are an international best practice and increasingly required by funders, including the Tri\-Agencies\. UBC supports the following resource to help you write a DMP:

-   [DMP Assistant](https://rdm.ubc.ca/data-management-plans/dmp-assistant): a national, purpose\-built tool with UBC\-specific guidance and templates for both pre\-award and post\-award plans\.

Visit the [Research Data Management](https://rdm.ubc.ca/) website or contact [research\.data@ubc\.ca](mailto:research.data@ubc.ca) to request a data management consultation with UBC Library\.

title: UBC Library FAQs
content_markdown:
UBC Library offers many services to Alumni, though the most common question is how Alumni can access library collections\. 

1.  Remote access to most UBC Library’s electronic resources is restricted by license agreement to current UBC students, faculty and staff\. [View a list of resources](http://guides.library.ubc.ca/az/databases?am=66) that have been licensed for UBC Alumni with remote access\. A CWL login is required for remote access; [follow these instructions](https://guides.library.ubc.ca/connect/openathens/alumni) if you are an alumni without a CWL\.
2.  UBC alumni who are able to visit campus can access additional licensed resources from one of the library’s public computers by using a guest OpenAthens login\. You can obtain a guest OpenAthens login in person at a library service desk; it will only provide access within a UBC Library location\.
3.  To borrow physical items, activate your Alumni library barcode through the *UBC Alumni app:* [View full instructions](https://services.library.ubc.ca/borrowing-services/get-library-access/alumni-cards/)
